questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I searched for an exchange spot in the second application round, so there were a limited number of places I could choose from.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was relatively easy to find information on McGill's website. They also answer emails pretty quick if you have any questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There were different welcome events were you could meet other exchange students and where you could get assistance if needed. I participated in these events, but didn't need further assistance.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I wish they had done more events throughout the semester, because they were all in the first week and at that time there were a lot of new things you had to learn, so would be nice with events later in the semester were you are not so overwhelmed.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. There are a lot of Facebook groups with people posting rooms for rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it was good to live off campus, because if you live on campus you have to buy a meal plan. Prices for rent were more or less the same as Copenhagen.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There were more of my courses where I had to search for pre-approval at the department. I think you can search this before they open for registration, so I would try to do this, because maybe you can't get the courses you thought. Be aware that they normal students all get to register two months before, so popular courses may already be filled up, and you only register for courses a month before you start. In the first 2 weeks there is an add-and-drop period so in this period you may be able to get a spot in some courses anyway.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You could email department and professors.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Somewhat succesfull. Because it is so late you register, my problem was that a lot of the courses that was pre-approved by UCPH was full, and I had to make a new reapproval which UCPH didn't approve before end of add-and-drop.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start the process in due time. If there are prerequisites maybe text the departments and ask they if it is possible to get the course anyway.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 300-500 level courses. 500 is both BA and MA courses as I understood.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More focus on active participation which is also part of the grade in some courses. As well as more assignments during the semester. I also had midterms in most of my courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Public sector economics 2, human motivation, communicating science and critical disability studies

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really liked the communicating science course since it was something quite different from my UCPH courses. I also really enjoyed critical disability studies. The professor was really great and inspiring, and it was an interesting perspective.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I had by Danish bank, so banking fees was quite expensive when I had to pay rent.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive than Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were all kinds of clubs. I think there were something for everyone.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: They have a sportscenter where I took workout classes, which was cheap and fun. I also went skiing with the skiing club. Went wine tasting with wine society and they also had a Nordic club doing fika. Mustbus was a really good organisation that do cheap bus trips.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Hike up on Mont Royal, see old town for historic buildings and la Plateu for vibrant neighborhood. Go hiking. Also visit other cities like Quebec City, Toronto, Ottawa.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I found it relatively easy. Know that people are speaking French, but at McGill everyone speaks English as well as young people and most older.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Maybe that signs are in French.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Campus culture were quite different from UCPH which was nice. A lot of clubs and social things.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Join some clubs. 
Academic level was the same or maybe a little bit easier than UCPH, so don't worry. 
Travel around and explore more than just Montreal.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting to have new experiences and travel around and meet different people as well as personal growth.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Sometimes it can be a bit hard making friends with locals since you are there for a short time

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
